contract: GET /notifications/:id/test sends the event test data of that record as one Apprise payload and answers 200, 400 when no Apprise URL is configured and 500 when the endpoint fails; an unknown id answers 404 and a non-admin is refused.

invariants.contract: GET /notifications/:id/test answers 200 with the text body OK and posts one Apprise payload {urls, title, body} rendered from that event's testData (not from a trigger), without changing lastFiredAt, numTimesFired, the failed-attempt counters or the settings row; it answers 500 when the Apprise endpoint rejects the payload with a non-2xx answer, when the record names an event the catalogue does not know, and when the endpoint does not answer within the six second client timeout.
exceptions: Named tests listed are relevant package-level current tests; their assertions do not yet prove every route branch or the complete upstream contract.

invariants.contract: GET /notifications/:id/test answers 401 without a token, 403 for the fixture non-admin user, 404 for an unknown id and 400 with the client-visible text Apprise is not configured when no Apprise URL is set, delivering nothing in every case.

exceptions: normal, error and edge facets are covered by the listed scenarios.
The 400 body text "Apprise is not configured" is asserted because the notification card shows error.response.data in a toast (client/components/cards/NotificationCard.vue:100-110).
The timeout assertion waits about six seconds because the Apprise client timeout is fixed at 6000 ms.

A record with an event name outside the six-entry catalogue is reachable only through the API (the edit modal offers the catalogue), and the route answers 500 for it; the scenario asserts only the status and that nothing was posted.
